templates.one_move_blunder: {played_san} hangs your {hung_piece} on {hung_square}, and after {opp_reply_san} you simply lose it for nothing; better was {best_san}, since {best_purpose}. Before you commit a move, check what your opponent can capture and count the trade first.
templates.walked_into_tactic: {front}; instead {best_san} was stronger because {best_purpose}, whereas {played_san} hands material away. Before any quiet move, check that it doesn't walk into a tactic that drops a piece.
templates.missed_free_material: {played_san} isn't a blunder, but {best_san} {win}, so you left material on the board. When an enemy piece sits undefended, grab it before making a quiet developing move.
templates.missed_mate: Instead of {played_san}, {best_san} was far stronger, throwing a forcing move at the exposed king and keeping the attack rolling. Always look hard at your checks and forcing moves before settling for a quieter line.
templates.allowed_mate: {played_san} lets your opponent force mate, so play {best_san} instead to shore up your king's safety. Before every move, ask what checks and captures your opponent gets.
templates.opening_knowledge: Your {played_san} brings the queen out too early, so Black can attack it with tempo and force a retreat while gaining development. Play {best_san} instead—it develops with purpose, fights for the center, and keeps your queen safe; develop your pieces before chasing with the queen.

good_move_templates.develop: {move} develops your {piece} toward the center and into the game — in the opening, get your knights and bishops off the back row early so you can castle and fight for the center.
good_move_templates.pawn: {move} fights for space and frees your other pieces to come out — in the opening, make moves that give your pieces room to join the game.
good_move_templates.capture: {move} wins free material — when an enemy piece sits undefended and it is safe to take, take it.
good_move_templates.other: {move} improves your {piece} onto a safer, more useful square — good habit: place each piece where it stays safe while doing the most work.
good_move_templates.castle: {move} castles your king to safety and brings a rook toward the center — castle early to get your king safe before the position opens up.
good_move_templates.centralize: {move} brings your {piece} to an active central square where it controls more of the board — put your pieces on central squares where they do the most work.
good_move_templates.queen_safety: {move} retreats your {piece} off the open line onto a calm, safe square connected to your other pieces — when a piece feels exposed, move it to safety before pushing forward.
good_move_templates.space: {move} grabs space on that side of the board and gives your pieces more room — when a pawn push gains space safely, it is usually worth playing.
good_move_templates.luft: {move} gives your king a little breathing room and denies your opponent a useful square — when nothing is urgent, quietly improving your king's safety is a good move.
good_move_templates.rook_activity: {move} swings your {piece} onto a real target instead of leaving it idle — put your rooks where they stay mobile and threaten something.
good_move_templates.rook_open_file: {move} seizes an open file where your {piece} controls the most squares — place your rooks on open files (columns with no pawns), where they reach the farthest.

opp_move_templates.develop: {move} brings the opponent's {piece} into the game — keep pace: develop your own pieces and get your king castled.
opp_move_templates.pawn: {move} grabs space for the opponent and frees their pieces — answer by fighting for the center and getting your own pieces active.
opp_move_templates.other: {move} improves the opponent's {piece} — stay alert to their plan and keep your own pieces active and defended.
opp_move_templates.castle: {move} tucks the opponent's king to safety — they can play freely now, so make sure your own king is safe too.
opp_move_templates.centralize: {move} plants the opponent's {piece} on an active central square — note what it now attacks and keep those squares defended.
opp_move_templates.queen_safety: {move} tucks the opponent's {piece} back to safety — no free attack on it now, so carry on with your own plan.
opp_move_templates.space: {move} grabs space for the opponent on that side — meet it by striking in the center or claiming space of your own.
opp_move_templates.luft: {move} gives the opponent's king an escape square — no back-rank tricks there now, so look elsewhere for your plan.
opp_move_templates.rook_activity: {move} activates the opponent's {piece} on a target — watch what it threatens and keep that area defended.
opp_move_templates.rook_open_file: {move} swings the opponent's {piece} onto an open file — contest the file with your own rook before they dominate it.
